title: The Lighter Brief
overview: Big civic news leads today: Mary Peltola won Alaska's Senate race, the last one to be called, closing out a strong midterm for Democrats. Closer to home in Charlotte, Duke Energy bills are going up, though by less than first requested, and a couple of tiny earthquakes gave folks a surprise boom. For the feel-good corner, Voyager 1 just hit a cosmic milestone and volunteers are delivering 2,000 Thanksgiving meals.

stories.headline: Mary Peltola wins Alaska's Senate seat, the last race called
stories.summary: Democrat Mary Peltola beat Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan, making her the first Alaska Native U.S. senator and capping a strong midterm for Democrats. The race got extra attention because a second candidate, Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., was also on the ballot. Republicans said that may have confused voters, and President Trump called the race 'rigged.' A BBC Verify analysis found that even combining both Sullivans' votes wouldn't have overcome Peltola's lead.
key_facts: Peltola reached 50.1% with 99% of votes counted, so no ranked-choice tally was needed
Democrats flipped 9 Senate seats, the most in a midterm since 1958, and will have 56 senators
A New York Times report alleged Democratic operatives tried to recruit 'spoiler' candidates; Peltola and Sullivan Jr. deny any link
Trump won Alaska by 13 points in 2024
disputed: The 'spoiler' recruitment claim comes from New York Times reporting that the BBC has not independently verified. Experts note the tactic wouldn't be illegal even if it happened.
A Republican legal challenge over the two Sullivans was unsuccessful.
stories.why: It finalizes the balance of power in Congress and marks a historic first for Alaska Native representation.

stories.headline: Duke Energy bills will rise in January, but less than Duke asked for
stories.summary: North Carolina regulators approved Duke Energy rate increases starting Jan. 1, 2027. The hike is roughly half of the original request after the state Attorney General's Office got involved. Regulators also set new rules so big data centers cover more of the cost of the power infrastructure built for them. Outlets report the numbers a bit differently: WSOC cites about 9.5% and roughly $11 more a month by 2028, while Duke's own figures show residential increases of about 4.7–4.8%.
key_facts: Duke Energy Carolinas typical bill: +$9.62/month on Jan. 1, 2027, then +$5.89 on Jan. 1, 2028
Duke Energy Progress typical bill: +$6.53/month in 2027, then +$4.66 in 2028
Duke originally sought about 18% for residential customers
New data center rules require large users to pay a premium and cover costs even if they leave early
stories.why: It's a real change to household budgets, and the data center rules aim to keep those costs from landing on regular customers.

stories.headline: Tiny earthquakes give Iredell and Rowan a surprise 'boom'
stories.summary: Small earthquakes rattled the area north of Charlotte late Tuesday, with reported magnitudes of 2.4 and 2.2. Folks mostly heard them more than felt them, describing a thunder-like boom. One Statesville resident said his sleeping dog jumped up and barked right before the house shook.
key_facts: The USGS revised the Iredell County quake from 2.4 to 2.2
It struck at 11:05 p.m. Tuesday, about 4 miles west of Cleveland
Depth was about 1 km below the surface
NC's largest quake in 100 years was a 5.1 near Sparta in 2020
stories.why: A good reminder that North Carolina does get the occasional small quake, and that this one was harmless.

stories.headline: Semi-truck hits Uptown apartment parking deck; one person hurt
stories.summary: A tractor-trailer crashed into the parking deck entrance of the Alister apartments near Sixth and McDowell streets Wednesday morning. One person went to the hospital with injuries that are not life-threatening. The cause hasn't been released yet.
key_facts: Happened around 10:45–11 a.m. Wednesday
A Mazda SUV also had major damage
Traffic was congested in the area
stories.why: Handy to know if you travel through Uptown, and the good news is the injuries weren't serious.

stories.headline: Audit flags messy record-keeping for Hurricane Melissa relief in Jamaica
stories.summary: Jamaica's Auditor General found missing inventory, unrecorded donations and inconsistent figures in how the disaster agency ODPEM handled Hurricane Melissa relief supplies. Auditors also found expired crackers and insects in a warehouse. ODPEM has referred the matter to external investigators.
key_facts: Donation estimates ranged from $400 million to $5.5 billion before ODPEM settled on $6.3 billion in July 2026
About $780 million in shipments weren't on donation schedules
359 boxes of expired crackers were found, along with weevil-infested rice reported back in March
The report was tabled in Parliament on Tuesday
stories.why: It's about making sure donated aid actually reaches the people it was meant for, and an outside investigation is now underway.

stories.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin meet in China for a first-ever three-way summit
stories.summary: President Trump arrived in Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific (APEC) summit and was greeted on the tarmac by Xi Jinping. He also briefly greeted Vladimir Putin. The three leaders meet together Thursday for the first time, and a Trump–Putin one-on-one is planned too. Trade, tariffs, AI and a possible path to ending the war in Ukraine are among the expected topics.
key_facts: It's Trump and Putin's first in-person meeting since August 2025
The Kremlin says the trilateral talks are allotted 'no more than an hour'
Trump envoys Witkoff and Kushner meet Ukrainian and European officials in Berlin the same day
China says Europe must be included in any Ukraine peace talks
stories.why: How these three get along shapes trade and global stability, and any progress on peace would be welcome news.

stories.headline: Volunteers deliver 2,000 Thanksgiving meals to CMS families
stories.summary: What started years ago as a 100-turkey giveaway is now 2,000 meal boxes for Charlotte-Mecklenburg Schools families. Hendrick Automotive Group donated the food. Volunteers from CMS, police, banks and community groups are delivering boxes to schools, apartments and churches. One volunteer who once lived in his car said he's glad to be the one helping now.
key_facts: 2,000 boxes, up from 100 turkeys when it began
Food donated by Hendrick Automotive Group
Grocery meal deals for 10 people: Aldi under $39, Food Lion under $40, Harris Teeter $50
stories.why: Neighbors helping neighbors, plus some budget-friendly Thanksgiving tips.

stories.headline: Family foundation boosts UWI psychology scholarships by 65%
stories.summary: The Gore Family Foundation raised its yearly scholarship support at the University of the West Indies from US$10,000 to US$16,500. The fund honors the late Dr. Lisa Gore Seifart, a clinical psychologist. This year it will help nine postgraduate students in psychology and counselling.
key_facts: Support went from US$10,000 to US$16,500 for 2026/2027
It doubled from US$5,000 to US$10,000 in 2024
Nine postgraduate students will be helped this year
The endowment fund has run since 2020
stories.why: More trained counsellors and psychologists means more mental health support for Jamaican communities.
